title: Quarantine aggregation side-effects and modernize cache adapters
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
The console aggregation layer has accumulated cross-cutting side-effects and in-place mutation patterns that are causing intermittent P95/P99 spikes, elevated heap churn on worker processes, and coupling between GraphQL resolvers and legacy cache adapters. Several pager incidents in Q3/Q4 traced back to long tail requests that originate from mixed sync/async aggregation paths.

Goal:
- Isolate aggregation execution into independent worker domains with clear memory and CPU caps (quarantine), eliminating cross-request mutation of shared aggregation state.
- Introduce a compatibility shim for legacy cache adapters so new adapter implementation can be swapped behind a feature flag without touching existing resolvers.
- Reduce end-to-end P99 for /api/console/* aggregated queries by at least 30% and reduce worker peak RSS by ~20% under a standard dashboard load.

Approach / Implementation plan:
1) Introduce "aggregation domain" concept: lightweight in-process worker pools (N shards) with single-threaded execution for each shard to avoid concurrent mutation of in-memory rollups. Implement an admit queue with backpressure and simple priority hints for interactive vs batch queries.
2) Replace shared mutable aggregation caches with immutable snapshots and an append-only event buffer; snapshots are compacted off the hotpath to reduce allocation churn.
3) Build a cache adapter shim layer: adapter.v2 implements memory-safe APIs (get_bulk, prefetch_hint, invalidate_async). The shim translates existing adapter calls and emits warnings.
4) Roll out behind a feature flag and runtime config: start with low-traffic project routes and ramp after two hours of successful load tests.
5) Add metrics and tracing spans for: queue latency, shard hotstart times, snapshot compaction duration, adapter shim fallbacks, and memory allocations per request.
6) Replace one legacy adapter (redis-legacy) with adapter.v2 in staging; run full smoke and synthetic dashboard replay.

Acceptance criteria (must pass before closing):
- New aggregation domain reduces P99 for targeted endpoints by >=30% in synthetic replay and shows stable headroom in staging for 48h.
- Worker process RSS and GC events reduced by ~20% under the same load profile.
- No increase in error rate for console routes; end-to-end error ratio remains <= current baseline.
- Feature-flagged shim can be toggled off with zero downtime and immediate rollback path documented.
- Code review completed and one infra runbook update added to Runbooks (link in comments).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Quarantine admission queue adds latency for rare large batch requests. Mitigation: implement priority hint and bypass for retainers, and introduce a burst slot pool for controlled spikes.
- Risk: Shim introduces subtle semantic differences. Mitigation: extensive adapter compatibility tests (unit + integration) and telemetry compare mode for the first 24h.

Rollout and monitoring:
- Phase 1: Deploy to staging (feature flag off) and validate metrics.
- Phase 2: Toggle feature flag ON for internal beta teams (10% traffic) for 12h.
- Phase 3: Increase to 50% with monitoring runbook autopause triggers (CPU>85% or error rate +3x).
- Phase 4: Full ramp and postmortem window of 72h to capture regressions.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Quarantine+Aggregation+Domains
- Bench harness (replay + synthetic): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/console-aggregation-replay
- Draft PR for worker shard prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4451

Notes: This ticket is focused on the server-side change; companion tickets will handle SDK/console client backpressure hints and dashboard UX for rollout visibility.
comments: 2025-11-04 - Aisha Patel: Triage and initial write-up. Observed three incidents in Oct where tail latency > 6s for aggregated dashboard queries. Marked P1 due to repeated customer-facing slowdowns.

2025-11-05 - Devon Chen: Spike work completed. Prototype of aggregation shard pool implemented (branch: feat/aggregation-domains). Local synthetic replay shows 28% P99 reduction but with higher allocation churn. Need to add immutable snapshot path.

2025-11-06 - Marco Rivera (performance): Ran heap profile during replay. Root cause includes repeated deep copies inside legacy cache adapters. Suggested shim approach and adding get_bulk API to reduce per-key allocations. Added to plan.
2025-11-07 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4451 - contains admission queue, shard worker scaffolding, and initial metrics. Requesting review from @sara-j, @liam-nguyen.

2025-11-08 - QA: Added integration tests that run adapter compatibility smoke; found 2 cases where invalidate_async semantics differ. Patch in progress to update shim to preserve timestamp-based tombstones.

2025-11-10 - Devon Chen: Updated design to include feature flag gating and rollout plan. Running staging replay for 12h; preliminary staging numbers: P99 down 34%, worker RSS down 18% under 500 concurrent replay clients. Will expand to 50% traffic tomorrow.
Follow-ups: create ENG-324901 for SDK slowpath hints; create ENG-324902 for runbook updates and oncall training.
